title: A gas spreads until it occupies the whole vessel
summary: A gas has no amount of its own: it expands to the outline and the capacity of whatever holds it.
body: The same OpenStax chemistry chapter treats a gas as the state that adopts both the outline and the capacity of its vessel. The picture on the page is a balloon. If the gas did not occupy space, the balloon would stay limp instead of puffing out when filled. That is why a covered pot holds steam only until the lid is off. Flowers, Robinson, Langley, and Theopold, edition of 11 March 2015. This is the phase classification, not a numbered gas law.
